questions.question: Which option is a complete sentence?
questions.explanation: A sentence needs a complete thought with a subject and predicate.

questions.question: In "The artist painted a mural," what is the subject?
questions.explanation: The subject tells who or what the sentence is about.

questions.question: In "The artist painted a mural," what is the predicate?
questions.explanation: The predicate tells what the subject did.

questions.question: Which word is the verb in "The children laughed loudly"?
questions.explanation: Laughed is the action word.

questions.question: Which word is a noun in "Bright stars filled the sky"?
questions.explanation: Stars names things, so it is a noun.

questions.question: Which option best describes a sentence?
questions.explanation: The lesson explains sentences as complete thoughts.

questions.question: Which sentence has an object?
questions.explanation: The window receives the action opened.

questions.question: In "The dog chased the ball," what receives the action?
questions.explanation: The object receives the action of the verb.

questions.question: Which group contains a subject and a predicate?
questions.explanation: Birds is the subject and migrate is the predicate.

questions.question: Which word tells what the subject does in "Students study grammar"?
questions.explanation: Study is the verb in the predicate.

questions.question: Which option is a common noun?
questions.explanation: Teacher is a general name for a person.

questions.question: Which option is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: India names a specific country.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a verb as an action?
questions.explanation: Chopped is an action verb.

questions.question: In "Lena bought a notebook," what is the direct object?
questions.explanation: A notebook receives the action bought.

questions.question: Which word is the noun in "The quiet library closed early"?
questions.explanation: Library names a place.

questions.question: Which word is the verb in "The quiet library closed early"?
questions.explanation: Closed tells what the library did.

questions.question: Which option is an indirect object in "Ana gave Tom a pen"?
questions.explanation: Tom receives the direct object, a pen.

questions.question: Which question helps find the direct object?
questions.explanation: A direct object receives the verb action.

questions.question: Which sentence has no direct object?
questions.explanation: Slept does not transfer action to an object.

questions.question: Which option best identifies "homework" in "Ravi finished his homework"?
questions.explanation: Homework receives the action finished.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in "The green door opened"?
questions.explanation: Green modifies the noun door.

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in "She answered quickly"?
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies the verb answered.

questions.question: Which word is a determiner in "Those books are heavy"?
questions.explanation: Those points to which books.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a prepositional phrase?
options: The keys are on the table.
questions.explanation: On the table is a prepositional phrase.

questions.question: Which word is the preposition in "We walked through the park"?
questions.explanation: Through shows the relationship between walked and park.

questions.question: Which word is a conjunction in "I studied and passed"?
questions.explanation: And connects studied and passed.

questions.question: Which conjunction best completes "I wanted tea, ___ I made coffee"?
questions.explanation: But shows contrast.

questions.question: Which option is a coordinating conjunction?
questions.explanation: Or connects choices.

questions.question: Which phrase modifies where the action happened in "They met after lunch"?
questions.explanation: After lunch is a prepositional phrase showing time.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a connector?
options: She was tired, under she rested.
She was tired, so she rested.
She was tired, very she rested.
She was tired, the she rested.
questions.explanation: So connects cause and result.

questions.question: What person and number is "I"?
questions.explanation: I refers to the speaker alone.

questions.question: What person and number is "we"?
questions.explanation: We includes the speaker and at least one other person.

questions.question: What person is "you"?
questions.explanation: You addresses the listener or listeners.

questions.question: Which set is third person singular?
questions.explanation: He, she, and it refer to one subject being talked about.

questions.question: Which pronoun is third person plural?
questions.explanation: They refers to people or things being talked about.

questions.question: Which subject is third person singular?
questions.explanation: The cat is one thing being talked about.

questions.question: Which subject is first person plural?
questions.explanation: My brother and I includes the speaker.

questions.question: Which subject is second person plural?
questions.explanation: You all addresses multiple listeners.

questions.question: Which replacement is correct for "John and Mary"?
questions.explanation: John and Mary are third person plural.

questions.question: Which replacement is correct for "John and I"?
questions.explanation: John and I includes the speaker, so use we.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ breakfast every morning."
questions.explanation: She is third person singular, so eat becomes eats.

questions.question: Complete: "They ___ to school."
questions.explanation: They is third person plural, so use the base form walk.

questions.question: Complete: "It ___ during winter."
questions.explanation: It is third person singular, so snow becomes snows.

questions.question: Complete: "We ___ on Saturdays."
questions.explanation: We is first person plural, so use the base form work.

questions.question: Complete: "You ___ to take a break."
questions.explanation: You uses the base form in simple present.

questions.question: Complete: "He ___ TV every evening."
questions.explanation: He is third person singular, and watch takes es.

questions.question: Complete: "They ___ eat meat."
questions.explanation: They takes do not in simple present negatives.

questions.question: Complete: "___ she like pizza?"
questions.explanation: She is third person singular, so the helper is does.

questions.question: Why is "Does she likes pizza?" wrong?
options: The main verb must stay base form after does
questions.explanation: Does is conjugated, so like stays base form.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Does goes before he, and play stays base form.

rounds.title: To Be and Real Use Challenge

questions.question: Complete: "I ___ a student."
questions.explanation: I takes am.

questions.question: Complete: "We ___ ready to go."
questions.explanation: We takes are.

questions.question: Complete: "Steve ___ playing outside."
questions.explanation: Steve is third person singular, so use is.

questions.question: Complete: "It ___ so cold yesterday."
questions.explanation: Yesterday marks past time; it takes was.

questions.question: Complete: "Someone called you when you ___ running outside."
questions.explanation: Past continuous with you uses were.

questions.question: Complete: "You must ___ kidding me!"
questions.explanation: After must, use base form be.

questions.question: Complete: "We have ___ here for ages."
questions.explanation: Have needs the past participle been.

questions.question: In "I have never regretted my choice," what does the verb phrase show?
questions.explanation: Have never regretted connects past experience to the present.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct form of to be?
questions.explanation: They takes are.

questions.question: What should you check first before choosing a verb form?
questions.explanation: Subject first, then person, number, and time.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Liz is an accountant and she has a typical 8-5 job.
Liz are an accountant and she have a typical 8-5 job.
Liz is an accountant and she have a typical 8-5 job.
Liz are an accountant and she has a typical 8-5 job.
questions.explanation: Liz/she is third-person singular, so is and has are correct.

questions.question: Which subject takes the regular simple-present verb "works"?
questions.explanation: He is third-person singular, so a regular verb adds s.

questions.question: Complete: "We ___ every morning."
questions.explanation: We is plural, so the base form run is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "I ___ ready."
questions.explanation: The to be form with I in simple present is am.

questions.question: Complete: "They ___ ready."
questions.explanation: They takes are in simple present.

questions.question: What is the first step in subject-verb agreement?
options: Choose the verb that sounds fancy.
questions.explanation: The real subject controls the verb.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ every day."
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular, so works is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "You ___ every morning."
questions.explanation: You uses the base verb in simple present.

questions.question: Which pair is correct for to be?
questions.explanation: He takes is; we takes are.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct agreement?
options: The subject and verb matches in person and number.
The subject and verb match in person and number.
The subjects and verb matches in person and number.
The subject and verbs matching in person and number.
questions.explanation: A compound subject takes the plural verb match.

questions.question: Complete: "It ___ outside in winter."
questions.explanation: It is third-person singular.

questions.question: Complete: "My friends ___ nearby."
questions.explanation: Friends is plural, so live is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "Everyone ___ going to the party."
questions.explanation: Everyone is singular.

questions.question: Complete: "Each of the students ___ a laptop."
questions.explanation: Each is singular.

questions.question: Complete: "John, as well as his friends, ___ soccer."
questions.explanation: As well as his friends is extra information; John controls the verb.

questions.question: Complete: "The book, as well as the notes, ___ on the table."
questions.explanation: Book is the real singular subject.

questions.question: Complete: "My friend, along with her colleagues, ___ at the door."
questions.explanation: Along with her colleagues does not change the singular subject friend.

questions.question: Complete: "No one ___ to work 16 hours a day."
questions.explanation: No one is a singular indefinite pronoun.

questions.question: Complete: "Someone ___ left their bag."
questions.explanation: Someone is singular, so has is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: My sister, as well as her friends, love going to art galleries.
My sister, as well as her friends, are loving going to art galleries.
My sister, as well as her friends, have love going to art galleries.
My sister, as well as her friends, loves going to art galleries.
questions.explanation: The real subject is my sister.

questions.question: Complete: "A majority of the staff ___ in favor of the new policy."
questions.explanation: The lesson treats staff/majority as one unit in this example.

questions.question: Complete: "The team ___ preparing for the big game."
questions.explanation: Team is treated as one unit.

questions.question: Complete: "The family ___ going on vacation."
questions.explanation: Family is treated as a singular collective noun in American English.

questions.question: Complete: "The team ___ a lot of games."
questions.explanation: Team is singular here, so loses is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "Neither the cat nor the dogs ___ around the house."
questions.explanation: Dogs is closer to the verb and plural.

questions.question: Complete: "Either my teammates or the captain ___ the warm-up drills."
questions.explanation: Captain is closer and singular.

questions.question: Complete: "Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready."
questions.explanation: Students is closer and plural.

questions.question: Complete: "Neither the students nor the teacher ___ ready."
questions.explanation: Teacher is closer and singular.

questions.question: Complete: "There ___ many reasons for the delay."
questions.explanation: The real subject is many reasons, plural.

questions.question: Complete: "There ___ a book and two pens on the table."
questions.explanation: In the shown pattern, the verb agrees with the closest subject after there: a book.

questions.question: Complete: "There ___ two pens and a book on the table."
questions.explanation: The closest subject after there is two pens, plural.

questions.question: Complete: "A lot of the cake ___ gone."
questions.explanation: Cake is singular/uncountable, so is is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "A lot of the cakes ___ gone."
questions.explanation: Cakes is plural, so are is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "Some of the money ___ missing."
questions.explanation: Money is singular/uncountable.

questions.question: Complete: "Some of the people ___ missing."
questions.explanation: People is plural.

questions.question: Complete: "Ten dollars ___ a high price to pay for socks."
questions.explanation: Ten dollars is treated as one amount here.

questions.question: Which sentence is a routine or habit?
options: I go to the gym every day.
I went to the gym once yesterday.
I am going to the gym right now.
I will go to the gym next year.
questions.explanation: Every day signals a routine, so simple present is correct.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ coffee every morning."
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular, so add s.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a fact/truth?
options: Water is boiling in this cup right now.
Water will boil if heated tomorrow.
questions.explanation: General truths use simple present.

questions.question: Complete: "The Earth ___ the sun."
questions.explanation: The Earth is third-person singular, so orbit becomes orbits.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a scheduled event?
options: The train is leaving at this exact second.
questions.explanation: Scheduled timetable events can use simple present.

questions.question: Complete: "The meeting ___ at 10 a.m. tomorrow."
questions.explanation: Meeting is singular and the event is scheduled.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a permanent situation?
options: He is standing in New York right now.
He lived in New York last summer only.
He will live in New York if he moves.
questions.explanation: Simple present can describe stable situations.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ as a teacher."
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular.

questions.question: Which sentence gives directions?
options: You turn left at the traffic lights.
You are turning left right now.
questions.explanation: Directions often use simple present/base verb with you.

questions.question: Complete: "First, you ___ the flour to the bowl."
questions.explanation: Instructions with you use the base verb.

questions.question: What is the main subject check for simple present?
options: Is the noun after the verb singular?
questions.explanation: Third-person singular is the main trigger for s/es.

questions.question: Complete: "They ___ nearby."
questions.explanation: They is third-person plural, so use the base form.

questions.question: Choose the correct positive sentence.
options: I does work in an office.
I am work in an office.
questions.explanation: I uses the base verb in positive simple present.

questions.question: Choose the correct third-person singular positive sentence.
options: She do work in an office.
questions.explanation: She takes works.

questions.question: Complete: "I ___ not like coffee."
questions.explanation: I uses do not.

questions.question: Complete: "He ___ not like coffee."
questions.explanation: He uses does not plus base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative sentence.
options: She doesn't work in an office.
She doesn't works in an office.
She don't work in an office.
She is not work in an office.
questions.explanation: Does carries the agreement; work stays base form.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: Use do with you, then base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct third-person singular question.
questions.explanation: Use does with she, then base verb play.

questions.question: Which rule is correct for regular negatives and questions?
options: The main verb always adds s.
Do/does changes; the main verb stays base form.
questions.explanation: This is a major warning in the video.

questions.question: Choose the correct to-be negative.
questions.explanation: To be does not use do/does.

questions.question: Complete: "They ___ not ready."
questions.explanation: They takes are.

questions.question: Choose the correct to-be question.
questions.explanation: To be questions put am/is/are before the subject.

questions.question: Complete: "___ I late?"
questions.explanation: I uses am in a to-be question.

rounds.title: Negative Questions, WH Questions, and Spelling

questions.question: Choose the natural contracted negative question.
questions.explanation: Don't + subject + base verb is natural for regular verbs.

questions.question: Which short answer fits "Don't you like coffee?"
questions.explanation: Short answers to do questions reuse do/don't.

questions.question: Choose the correct short answer to "Doesn't he live here?"
questions.explanation: Use does for he.

questions.question: Choose the correct to-be negative question.
questions.explanation: To be uses is not/isn't without do/does.

questions.question: Which WH question is correct?
questions.explanation: WH + does + subject + base verb.

questions.question: Which question correctly uses who as the subject?
questions.explanation: When who is the subject, do/does is not used.

questions.question: Complete: "How often ___ you exercise?"
questions.explanation: How often follows the normal do/does question pattern.

questions.question: Complete: "How long ___ the movie last?"
questions.explanation: Movie is third-person singular, so use does plus base verb last.

questions.question: Complete: "He ___ TV."
questions.explanation: Watch ends in ch, so add es.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ the car."
questions.explanation: Fix ends in x, so add es.

questions.question: Complete: "He ___ English."
questions.explanation: Consonant + y changes to ies.

questions.question: Complete: "She ___ the piano."
questions.explanation: Vowel + y keeps y and adds s.

questions.question: Which simple-present form of to be fits "I"?
questions.explanation: I am is the memorized form.

questions.question: Which simple-present form of to be fits "he/she/it"?
questions.explanation: He/she/it is.

questions.question: Which simple-present form of to have fits "he"?
questions.explanation: He has is irregular and must be memorized.

questions.question: Where does "often" usually go with action verbs?
questions.explanation: She often plays tennis.

questions.question: Choose the correct frequency-adverb placement with to be.
questions.explanation: With am/is/are, frequency words usually come after the be verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct action-verb placement.
options: We are sometimes eat dinner out.
questions.explanation: With action verbs, frequency words usually come before the main verb.

questions.question: Which marker means 0% frequency?
questions.explanation: Never means not at all.

questions.question: Which marker means almost never?
questions.explanation: Rarely means it almost never happens.

questions.question: Choose the natural routine-marker sentence.
questions.explanation: Every morning usually goes at the end.

questions.question: Complete: "The bus leaves ___ 8 a.m."
questions.explanation: Use at with exact clock times.

questions.question: Complete: "I usually read ___ the evening."
questions.explanation: Use in with parts of the day.

questions.question: Complete: "We have a meeting ___ Tuesday."
questions.explanation: Use on with specific days.

rounds.title: Past Uses, Positive Forms, and Spelling

questions.question: What is the main use of the simple past tense in the lesson?
options: Actions completed at a specific point in the past
Actions happening at this exact moment
Plans that may happen in the future
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the simple past as the tense for actions completed at a specific point in the past.

questions.question: Which opening example is used in the video?
options: I visit my friend every day.
I am visiting my friend now.
I will visit my friend tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The video uses “I visited my friend yesterday” to show a finished past action.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly forms a regular positive simple-past statement?
options: I walk to the store yesterday.
I did walked to the store.
I was walk to the store.
questions.explanation: A regular positive statement uses the subject followed by the past form: walked.

questions.question: Which pair gives the two simple-past forms of to be?
questions.explanation: The irregular verb to be has the past forms was and were.

questions.question: Which subject-and-verb pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: We pairs with were; I and he/she/it pair with was.

questions.question: How does a regular verb that already ends in e form its past tense?
questions.explanation: A verb already ending in e adds only d: dance becomes danced.

questions.question: Which past-tense spelling is correct for study?
questions.explanation: With consonant + y, change y to i and add ed: studied.

questions.question: Why does played keep the letter y?
options: Play ends in a vowel followed by y.
Every verb ending in y keeps y.
The past tense never changes spelling.
questions.explanation: When a vowel comes before y, keep the y and add ed.

questions.question: Which one-syllable CVC spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Stop is a one-syllable CVC verb, so the final consonant doubles before ed.

questions.question: Why does preferred have two r letters before ed?
options: Every two-syllable verb doubles its last letter.
Every verb ending in r is irregular.
It ends in CVC and its final syllable is stressed.
questions.explanation: A multi-syllable CVC verb doubles the final consonant when the final syllable is stressed.

questions.question: Which list contains only irregular simple-past forms taught in the video?
questions.explanation: Go, have, and see have the irregular past forms went, had, and saw.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a time marker from the video correctly?
options: I traveled to Japan next year.
I travel to Japan last year.
I traveled to Japan last year.
I did traveled to Japan last year.
questions.explanation: Last year marks a completed past time, and traveled is the correct positive past form.

rounds.title: Past Negatives, Questions, and WH Forms

questions.question: What structure forms a negative sentence with an ordinary verb?
questions.explanation: Use subject + did not (or didn't) + the base form of the main verb.

questions.question: Why does go remain in the base form in “I didn't go to the party”?
options: Did already carries the past tense.
Go is always a present-tense verb.
The sentence is actually future tense.
Party prevents the verb from changing.
questions.explanation: Only one verb needs to carry the past marking; did carries it, so go stays in the base form.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: A simple-past question uses did + subject + base verb.

questions.question: Which is the correct negative form with to be?
options: They were not ready for the test.
They did not were ready for the test.
They were did not ready for the test.
They not were ready for the test.
questions.explanation: With to be, use subject + was/were + not and do not add did.

questions.question: How does the video form a past question with to be?
questions.explanation: Invert the past form of to be and the subject: Was I...? Were they...?

questions.question: Which question asks correctly about the results?
options: Did they were happy with the results?
Was they happy with the results?
Were they happy with the results?
They were happy with the results?
questions.explanation: They takes were, and a question puts were before the subject.

questions.question: What can a negative question express according to the lesson?
options: Surprise, confirmation, or a polite offer
questions.explanation: The instructor presents surprise, confirmation, and polite offers or suggestions as common uses.

questions.question: Which negative question normally sounds more natural?
options: Did you no see the movie?
Did not you saw the movie?
Were you not see the movie?
questions.explanation: The contracted form “Didn't you...” is described as the more natural form.

questions.question: What is a correct short answer to “Didn't she call you?”
questions.explanation: A short answer to a did question reuses did: Yes, she did.

questions.question: What is the usual structure for a simple-past WH question?
options: WH word + subject + did + past verb
Did + WH word + subject + past verb
WH word + was + subject + base verb
WH word + did + subject + base verb
questions.explanation: Most WH questions use WH word + did + subject + base verb.

questions.question: What is special about a question when who is the subject?
options: It uses a past main verb without did.
questions.explanation: When who is the subject, use the past form directly, as in “Who wrote this book?”

questions.question: Which question asks about a countable number?
options: How much emails did you send?
How many emails did you send?
How long emails did you send?
How far emails did you send?
questions.explanation: How many is used for countable items such as emails.

questions.question: Which sentence answers the video's first review question?
options: I will visit my friend tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Visited is a regular past form, and yesterday is a past-time marker.

questions.question: How does the review form a negative with a regular verb?
questions.explanation: Use did not or didn't followed by the base main verb.

questions.question: Why is “didn't + past verb” incorrect?
options: Did already carries past tense, so the main verb stays base form.
questions.explanation: Changing both verbs would mark the past tense twice.

questions.question: Which option is the irregular past verb in the review list?
questions.explanation: Went is the irregular past form of go.

questions.question: Which complete sentence does the video identify as correct?
options: She didn't went to the store.
I am going to the park yesterday.
questions.explanation: Played and yesterday correctly express a completed past action.

questions.question: How should “She didn't went to the store” be corrected?
options: She didn't go to the store.
She doesn't went to the store.
She wasn't go to the store.
She didn't goes to the store.
questions.explanation: After didn't, use the base form go.

questions.question: Why is “They was at the party” incorrect?
options: The plural subject they uses were.
questions.explanation: They pairs with the past form were.

questions.question: Which simple-past question is correct?
options: Did she went to the store?
Did he goes to the gym?
questions.explanation: The pattern is did + subject + base verb.

questions.question: Complete: “She ___ (go) to the store yesterday.”
questions.explanation: Go is irregular; its positive simple-past form is went.

questions.question: Complete: “They ___ (not, finish) the project on time.”
questions.explanation: A regular negative uses did not followed by finish.

questions.question: Complete: “He ___ (be) late for the meeting.”
questions.explanation: The subject he pairs with was.

questions.question: What irregular past form of eat appears in the video?
questions.explanation: The video sentence says Jake ate tons of fast food as a kid.

questions.question: Why is cried spelled with ied?
questions.explanation: For consonant + y, replace y with i and add ed.

questions.question: Why does stayed keep y?
questions.explanation: With vowel + y, keep y and add ed.

questions.question: Why does dropped contain two p letters?
options: Drop follows the one-syllable CVC rule.
questions.explanation: The final consonant doubles before ed in this CVC verb.

questions.question: Which combined to be sentence matches the exercise?
options: I was hungry, but my friends were not eager to join me.
I were hungry, but my friends was not eager.
I did be hungry, but my friends didn't be eager.
I am hungry, but my friends are not eager yesterday.
questions.explanation: I uses was, while the plural subject my friends uses were.

questions.question: Why does my friends use were?
options: My friends is plural and can be replaced by they.
Were is the past of do.
questions.explanation: My friends is plural, equivalent to they, which pairs with were.

questions.question: Which time markers are identified in the final sentence?
options: last night and three weeks ago
questions.explanation: Both phrases explicitly locate events in past time.

questions.question: Complete: Nick's mother ___ to stay at home, so she ___ for Spanish classes.
questions.explanation: Use didn't + base verb want, while the positive regular verb becomes signed up.

questions.question: Which question correctly completes the third exercise?
options: Where did you were last night?
questions.explanation: A question with to be inverts were and you.

questions.question: Complete: I ___ calling you, but you ___ the phone.
questions.explanation: Try becomes tried, and didn't is followed by the base phrasal verb pick up.

questions.question: How does the video correct 'Kim goed ... the last night'?
options: Kim went on a date with David last night.
Kim goed on a date with David last night.
Kim did went on a date with David the last night.
Kim was go on a date with David last night.
questions.explanation: Go becomes went, and the phrase is last night without the.

questions.question: What simple-past form of drive is used in the Houston sentence?
questions.explanation: Drove is simple past; driven is the past participle.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes drove and driven?
options: Drove is simple past; driven is a past participle.
questions.explanation: The correction uses I drove; driven is not the standalone simple-past form.

rounds.title: Will: Uses, Statements, Negatives, and Questions

questions.question: Which is one of the four simple-future uses listed at the start of the video?
questions.explanation: The opening overview lists predictions, decisions, promises or offers, and future facts.

questions.question: Which prediction appears in the video?
questions.explanation: The video uses will + base verb in 'It will rain tomorrow.'

questions.question: What structure forms a positive sentence with will?
questions.explanation: A positive simple-future statement uses subject + will + base verb.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly makes an offer from the lesson?
options: I helping you carry your bags.
I will to help you carry your bags.
I will helped you carry your bags.
I will help you carry your bags.
questions.explanation: The offer uses I will followed by the base verb help.

questions.question: Which future fact is shown in the video?
options: The sun will rise at 6 a.m.
The sun will rises at 6 a.m.
The sun is rise at 6 a.m.
questions.explanation: The video uses 'The sun will rise at 6 a.m.' as a future fact.

questions.question: What is the contraction of 'they will'?
questions.explanation: Will contracts to 'll, so they will becomes they'll.

questions.question: Which formula forms a negative future sentence?
questions.explanation: Use subject + will not (won't) + base verb.

questions.question: Which negative example matches the lesson?
options: They don't will finish the project.
They will not to finish the project.
They won't finish the project on time.
questions.explanation: Won't is followed by the base form finish.

questions.question: How is a yes/no future question formed?
questions.explanation: Put will before the subject and keep the main verb in its base form.

questions.question: Which polite request appears in the video?
options: Do you will help me with homework?
Will you help me with my homework?
Will you helped me with my homework?
Are you help me with my homework?
questions.explanation: Will you + base verb makes the polite request shown.

questions.question: What can 'Won't she call you tomorrow?' express?
options: Surprise because the speaker thought she would
questions.explanation: The negative-question table presents this sentence as an expression of surprise.

questions.question: Which is a correct short answer to 'Won't she be here tomorrow?'
questions.explanation: A short answer to a will question reuses will: Yes, she will.

rounds.title: Future WH Questions, Markers, Shall, and Going To

questions.question: What is the usual WH-question order?
options: Will + WH word + subject + base verb
WH word + will + subject + base verb
questions.explanation: Use WH word + will + subject + base verb.

questions.question: Which answer does the video give for 'Where will she travel next?'
questions.explanation: The sample answer uses will + base verb travel and names Mexico.

questions.question: Which question asks about a countable number?
questions.explanation: How many asks about countable nouns such as people.

questions.question: Which set contains only future time markers highlighted in the video?
options: tomorrow / next year / soon / in a few days
questions.explanation: All four phrases are presented as future time markers.

questions.question: Where does the lesson say shall is especially likely to appear?
options: Formal speech, legal documents, rules, and polite expressions
questions.explanation: The video describes shall as less common but still useful in formal, legal, and polite contexts.

questions.question: What does shall indicate in the contract example?
questions.explanation: In contracts, rules, or laws, shall can mark an obligation.

questions.question: Which modern-English statement replaces the traditional 'We shall arrive at noon'?
questions.explanation: The video says will has almost completely replaced shall in general future statements.

questions.question: What does going to commonly express in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Going to is introduced for plans and intentions.

questions.question: Which planned-future sentence appears in the video?
options: I going to start a project.
I am going to start a new project next week.
I will going to start a project.
I am going start a project.
questions.explanation: The correct structure is am + going to + base verb start.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say 'It is going to rain' after mentioning black clouds?
options: The prediction is based on present evidence.
Shall cannot be used with weather.
questions.explanation: The black clouds provide visible evidence for the prediction.

questions.question: Which going-to question is formed correctly?
options: Where going she to travel next?
Where does she going to travel next?
Where she is going to travel next?
Where is she going to travel next?
questions.explanation: Invert is and she, then use going to + base verb.

questions.question: When can the simple present describe the future?
questions.explanation: The lesson uses the simple present for schedules and fixed future events.

questions.question: Which scheduled-future example appears in the video?
options: The train will leaving at six.
The train leaves at 6 p.m. tomorrow.
The train is leave at six.
questions.explanation: The train schedule uses the simple-present verb leaves with a future time marker.

questions.question: What future meaning does the present continuous express here?
questions.explanation: The video uses present continuous for arranged future activities.

questions.question: Which arranged-future sentence matches the video?
options: We are meeting them tomorrow at 6 p.m.
questions.explanation: The arrangement uses are + meeting and a future time expression.

questions.question: Which form best fits a timetable?
questions.explanation: The lesson assigns scheduled or fixed events to the simple present.

questions.question: Which comparison best summarizes the lesson?
options: Will is only for schedules; going to is only for laws.
Will handles general future meanings; going to highlights plans or evidence; present forms cover schedules or arrangements.
Every future sentence must contain will.
Shall is the only normal future form in modern English.
questions.explanation: The video closes by distinguishing will, going to, scheduled simple present, and arranged present continuous.

questions.question: Which sentence does the video identify as simple future?
options: I will finish my homework tomorrow.
I am finishing my homework now.
I had finished my homework last week.
questions.explanation: Will + the base verb finish forms the simple future, and tomorrow supplies a future time marker.

questions.question: Which negative sentence is correct?
options: I didn't will go to the party.
I will not went to the party.
I will not go to the party.
I won't will go to the party.
questions.explanation: A future negative uses will not followed by the base verb go.

questions.question: Which future question follows the pattern taught in the video?
options: Will you go to the meeting tomorrow?
Do you will go to the meeting tomorrow?
Did you will go to the meeting tomorrow?
Are you will go to the meeting tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Future questions invert will and the subject, then use the base verb.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'going to' for a plan?
options: I will going to finish my project tonight.
I going to finish my project tonight.
I am going finish my project tonight.
I am going to finish my project tonight.
questions.explanation: Going to requires the agreeing form am, followed by going to and the base verb finish.

questions.question: Why is 'I will going to finish' incorrect?
options: Will and going to should not be combined in that structure.
Finish must always be past tense.
Tonight can only describe the past.
The subject I cannot discuss plans.
questions.explanation: Scott explicitly warns not to put will and going to together.

questions.question: How does the video complete the fixed-schedule sentence about the plane?
options: The plane will leaving at 8 a.m. next Monday.
The plane leaves at 8 a.m. next Monday.
The plane left at 8 a.m. next Monday.
The plane is leave at 8 a.m. next Monday.
questions.explanation: A scheduled future event can use the simple present: the plane leaves.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'shall' as the suggestion shown in the review?
options: Shall we go? It's getting late.
We shall going? It's getting late.
Do shall we go? It's getting late.
Shall we went? It's getting late.
questions.explanation: The video completes the suggestion as Shall we go? with shall before we and the base verb go.

questions.question: Which transformed sentence is correct for '(They / not to go) to the bar tomorrow'?
options: They not will go to the bar tomorrow.
They will not went to the bar tomorrow.
They will not go to the bar tomorrow.
They do not will go to the bar tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Put will after the subject, not after will, and keep go in its base form.

questions.question: Where does 'probably' go in 'I will ___ meet up with some friends'?
questions.explanation: The instructor moves probably after will and before the base verb: I will probably meet up.

questions.question: Which contracted sentence correctly completes 'I (to call) you later'?
questions.explanation: I'll is the contraction of I will and is followed by the base verb call.

questions.question: Which contracted sentence correctly completes the negative advice exercise?
options: I don't will do anything without your advice.
I won't do anything without your advice.
I won't did anything without your advice.
I'll not did anything without your advice.
questions.explanation: Won't replaces will not and is followed by the base verb do.

questions.question: What is the time marker in 'He'll finish his book in a week or two'?
questions.explanation: In a week or two tells when the future action is expected to finish.

questions.question: What is the probability marker in 'You probably won't listen to me'?
questions.explanation: Probably expresses the speaker's estimate of likelihood.

questions.question: Which activity will Mike probably do after work?
questions.explanation: Mike says, 'I'll probably play some video games after work.'

questions.question: What does Mike definitely say he will not do tomorrow?
questions.explanation: His line is, 'I definitely won't go out with my friends tomorrow.'

questions.question: Which phrase expresses Mike's strongest certainty about starting another language?
questions.explanation: Mike says, 'I'll most certainly start learning another language.'

questions.question: Complete: 'Why can't you come over? I ___ you sleep at my place.'
questions.explanation: The revealed answer is, 'I'll let you sleep at my place.'

questions.question: Which restaurant suggestion matches the revealed answer?
options: Will we went to the restaurant tonight?
Do shall we go to the restaurant tonight?
We shall going to the restaurant tonight?
Shall we go to the restaurant tonight?
questions.explanation: A suggestion uses shall before we and the base verb go.

questions.question: Which negative prediction is offered about robots?
options: Robots won't take over the planet.
Robots won't took over the planet.
Robots not will take over the planet.
questions.explanation: The sample answer uses won't followed by the base verb take.

questions.question: What does “continuous” remind the learner to add to the main verb?
questions.explanation: The opening memory aid links every continuous tense with an -ing main verb.

questions.question: Which structure forms a positive present-continuous sentence?
questions.explanation: The tense combines an agreeing present form of to be with an -ing main verb.

questions.question: Which sentence describes an action happening now?
questions.explanation: Is eating is the present-continuous form used for the current action.

questions.question: Which example shows a temporary action?
options: She is working on a new project this week.
questions.explanation: This week frames the work as a temporary current activity.

questions.question: Which sentence uses present continuous for a future arrangement?
options: We are meeting them at 6 p.m. tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Are meeting plus a specific future time expresses a confirmed arrangement.

questions.question: Where does “always” go in “He is always losing his keys”?
questions.explanation: Always follows the form of to be and precedes the -ing verb.

questions.question: Which form agrees with the subject I?
questions.explanation: I takes am: I am studying.

questions.question: Which form agrees with she?
questions.explanation: Third-person singular she takes is.

questions.question: How is a negative present-continuous statement formed?
options: Put did not before the subject
Add not after the -ing verb only
questions.explanation: The negative structure is subject + am/is/are + not + verb-ing.

questions.question: Which negative contraction does not exist in standard English?
questions.explanation: The lesson explicitly notes that am not has no standard contraction.

questions.question: Which question uses inversion correctly?
options: Are you coming to the party?
Are coming you to the party?
questions.explanation: The question switches are and the subject you.

questions.question: Which is a correct negative question?
questions.explanation: Without a contraction, use am + subject + not + verb-ing.

rounds.title: Negative Questions, WH Forms, and Time Markers

questions.question: What can “Isn’t she working today?” express?
questions.explanation: The lesson lists surprise as one use of negative questions.

questions.question: Which negative question acts as a confirmation check?
options: Aren't they coming to the meeting?
questions.explanation: The speaker checks whether they are coming.

questions.question: How can you answer “Aren’t you studying?” positively?
questions.explanation: A direct question with you changes perspective to I in the answer.

questions.question: What is the normal WH-question structure?
questions.explanation: The WH word comes first, followed by the agreeing form of to be, subject, and -ing verb.

questions.question: Which question asks for a destination?
questions.explanation: Where asks about location or destination.

questions.question: What does “how many” ask about?
questions.explanation: How many is used with countable people or things.

questions.question: Why is “Who is helping you?” structurally special?
options: Who is an object after the verb.
questions.explanation: Who occupies the subject position, so no separate subject follows is.

questions.question: Which marker means the exact current moment?
questions.explanation: At the moment is grouped with now and right now.

questions.question: Where does “currently” naturally go?
options: After am/is/are and before the -ing verb
questions.explanation: The neutral placement is She is currently reading.

questions.question: What does placing a time marker first usually add?
questions.explanation: Initial placement focuses or emphasizes the time phrase.

questions.question: Which is normally a stative use?
options: I am seeing the doctor tomorrow.
I am thinking about the problem.
questions.explanation: Know expresses a state and normally stays in the simple present.

questions.question: When can “have” be continuous?
options: When it means an action such as eating lunch
questions.explanation: Having lunch describes an activity, unlike having a car as possession.

rounds.title: ING Spelling, Stative Verbs, and Changing Meaning

questions.question: How is write changed before adding -ing?
questions.explanation: Drop the final silent e and add -ing.

questions.question: Which spelling follows the one-syllable CVC rule?
questions.explanation: Run is one syllable and ends consonant-vowel-consonant, so n doubles.

questions.question: Why does begin become beginning?
options: Its final CVC syllable is stressed.
questions.explanation: A multi-syllable CVC verb doubles when the final syllable is stressed.

questions.question: How does lie form its -ing spelling?
questions.explanation: Change final ie to y, then add -ing.

questions.question: Which British/American pair matches the lesson?
questions.explanation: British English commonly doubles final l, while American English does not when the last syllable is unstressed.

questions.question: Which is normally a stative use?
options: I am seeing the doctor tomorrow.
I am thinking about the problem.
questions.explanation: Know expresses a state and normally stays in the simple present.

questions.question: When can “have” be continuous?
options: When it means an action such as eating lunch
questions.explanation: Having lunch describes an activity, unlike having a car as possession.

questions.question: Which sentence uses see as a planned meeting?
options: I am seeing the doctor tomorrow.
I am seeing what you mean.
questions.explanation: Seeing the doctor means meeting the doctor at an appointment.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses an opinion rather than an ongoing mental activity?
options: I am thinking about the problem.
I think it's a good idea.
questions.explanation: Think meaning opinion is stative; thinking about a problem is an activity.

questions.question: Which summary is correct?
options: Every verb can always be continuous.
Present continuous only means this exact second.
The main verb agrees directly with the subject.
Use agreeing am/is/are plus verb-ing, while checking meaning, spelling, and stative exceptions.
questions.explanation: This captures the form, varied uses, spelling rules, and non-continuous exceptions taught in the video.

questions.question: How does have become having?
questions.explanation: The review explicitly points out have → having.

questions.question: Which final answer describes an ongoing change?
options: The economic situation is getting worse.
questions.explanation: Is getting describes a situation changing in the current period.

questions.question: Complete: They ___ for their exams right now.
questions.explanation: They takes are and study becomes studying.

questions.question: Complete the negative: I ___ TV at the moment.
questions.explanation: Use am not followed by watching.

questions.question: Complete: She ___ on a new project this week.
questions.explanation: She agrees with is and work takes -ing.

questions.question: Complete the arrangement: We ___ them for dinner tomorrow.
questions.explanation: We takes are, and tomorrow signals the arrangement.

questions.question: Where is always placed in the wallet exercise?
questions.explanation: The answer is He is always forgetting his wallet.

questions.question: Which complete multi-subject sentence matches the review?
options: I is frying; mom are washing; brothers is waiting.
I frying; mom washing; brothers waiting.
I am frying; mom is washing; brothers are waiting.
I am fry; mom is wash; brothers are wait.
questions.explanation: Each form of to be agrees independently with its subject.

questions.question: How does the weather question begin?
questions.explanation: The question inverts is and dummy subject it.

questions.question: Which contracted negative answers that weather question?
questions.explanation: Is not contracts to isn’t.

questions.question: Which current-period marker is identified in Samantha’s exercise?
questions.explanation: The review identifies this year as the time marker.

questions.question: Which final answer describes an ongoing change?
options: The economic situation is getting worse.
questions.explanation: Is getting describes a situation changing in the current period.

questions.question: Which question order is correct?
options: Why are you wearing a coat?
Why you are wearing a coat?
questions.explanation: Direct questions place are before the subject you.

questions.question: What is embedded inside “Do you know what your family is doing now?”
questions.explanation: What your family is doing is an embedded present-continuous clause.

questions.question: Which sentence describes an action in progress at a specific past moment?
options: I was reading at 6 p.m. yesterday.
questions.explanation: Was reading places the speaker inside an ongoing action at a past time.

questions.question: Which form creates the past continuous?
questions.explanation: Use the matching past form of to be plus the -ing form.

questions.question: Choose the correct agreement.
questions.explanation: They takes were.

questions.question: Choose the correct agreement for “she.”
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular and takes was.

questions.question: Which sentence shows an interrupted action?
options: I was cooking when the phone rang.
I am cooking while she reads.
questions.explanation: Was cooking is the longer action; rang is the interrupting simple-past event.

questions.question: Which sentence shows two parallel past actions?
options: I was studying while they were playing.
I studied when they were playing.
I will study while they play.
questions.explanation: Both simultaneous actions use past continuous and are linked by while.

questions.question: What normally follows “when” in an interrupted-action pattern?
questions.explanation: When usually introduces the shorter event in the simple past.

questions.question: What normally follows “while” in this lesson’s action pattern?
questions.explanation: While introduces an action in progress.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative form.
questions.explanation: Put not after was/were and before the -ing verb.

questions.question: What is the contraction of “was not”?
questions.explanation: Was not contracts to wasn't.

questions.question: What is the contraction of “were not”?
questions.explanation: Were not contracts to weren't.

questions.question: Choose the correctly inverted question.
questions.explanation: Move were before the subject.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the past continuous?
options: She studies when the bell rings.
She studied when the bell rang.
She was studying when the bell rang.
She will study when it rings.
questions.explanation: Was + studying forms the past continuous.

questions.question: What is the negative of “He was watching TV”?
questions.explanation: Add not between was and watching.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an interrupted action?
options: She was cooking when the phone rang.
She is cooking when the phone rings.
questions.explanation: The phone rang during the ongoing cooking action.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses two parallel past actions?
options: I was studying while they were playing soccer.
I was studying while they are playing.
questions.explanation: Both simultaneous actions use was/were + -ing.

questions.question: Which is NOT a typical use of past continuous?
options: An action at a specific past time
questions.explanation: Present continuous—not past continuous—can describe arranged future plans.

questions.question: Complete: “They ___ on the phone when the doorbell rang.”
questions.explanation: They agrees with were.

questions.question: Complete: “I ___ when you called.”
questions.explanation: I takes was; not comes before sleeping.

questions.question: Complete: “He ___ while his sister ___ TV.”
questions.explanation: Both singular subjects take was in parallel continuous actions.

questions.question: Complete: “She ___ when she ___ her ankle.”
questions.explanation: The running was ongoing; the twist was the shorter simple-past event.

questions.question: Complete: “We ___ for the bus at 7 p.m. yesterday.”
questions.explanation: We takes were.

questions.question: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Get is a one-syllable CVC verb, so double t.

questions.question: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Drop the final silent e before adding -ing.

questions.question: Why was Sam trying to reach Nate?
questions.explanation: Sam begins by asking where Nate was yesterday.

questions.question: What was Nate working on?
questions.explanation: Nate says he was working on a project.

questions.question: Who was Nate talking to?
questions.explanation: He says he was talking to a local policeman.

questions.question: Who else was Nate interviewing?
questions.explanation: He was interviewing strangers in the streets.

questions.question: What happened while Nate was interviewing an old lady?
options: A cop came up to him.
questions.explanation: A cop approached during the ongoing interview.

questions.question: What did the cop want to see?
questions.explanation: The cop wanted to see his identification.

questions.question: Did Nate finish the project?
questions.explanation: He answers “Thankfully, yes.”

questions.question: How long was Nate working on it?
questions.explanation: The whole day is the duration stated.

questions.question: Which phrase is a past-continuous WH-question?
questions.explanation: Were + subject + doing is past continuous.

questions.question: What is the function of “while” in the story?
questions.explanation: While introduces the background action in progress.

questions.question: Why is “came up” in the simple past?
options: It is the completed event occurring during the interview.
questions.explanation: The cop’s approach is the shorter completed event.

questions.question: Which phrase emphasizes duration?
questions.explanation: The whole evening says how long Sam was trying.

questions.question: Choose the lesson answer: “Last summer I ___ in the river every day.”
questions.explanation: The lesson uses was swimming to frame the repeated summer activity as ongoing background.

questions.question: Complete: “While I ___ a shower, the phone rang.”
questions.explanation: While introduces the ongoing shower action.

questions.question: Choose the correct simple-past form of “ring.”
questions.explanation: Rang is the simple past form.

questions.question: Complete: “Anne ___ a cup when she was washing the dishes.”
questions.explanation: Broke is the shorter completed event.

questions.question: Complete: “Anne broke a cup when she ___ the dishes.”
questions.explanation: The dishwashing was already in progress.

questions.question: Complete: “Sally was working on her thesis ___ eight o’clock.”
questions.explanation: Use at with a clock time.

questions.question: Complete: “Tom was sleeping ___ his mom took a picture.”
questions.explanation: When introduces the shorter simple-past action.

questions.question: Complete: “I was living in Italy ___ 2009.”
questions.explanation: Use in with a year.

questions.question: Complete: “A burglar broke in ___ they were watching TV.”
questions.explanation: While introduces the ongoing TV-watching action.

questions.question: Which answer fits “What were you doing at 5 p.m. last night?”
questions.explanation: Was watching correctly reports an activity in progress.

questions.question: Which answer correctly combines a phone call with an ongoing action?
options: I was having a bath when I heard the phone.
I had a bath while I was heard the phone.
I were bathing when I hear it.
questions.explanation: The bath is ongoing; heard is the shorter simple-past event.

questions.question: Choose the correct family answer.
options: My family were spending time at the beach.
My family was spending time at the beach.
questions.explanation: In the lesson, family is treated as a singular collective noun and takes was.

questions.question: What is the core future-continuous structure?
questions.explanation: Use will be followed by the -ing form.

questions.question: Which sentence shows an action in progress at a future time?
options: I will be traveling at this time next week.
questions.explanation: Will be traveling places the action in progress at that future moment.

questions.question: Which sentence emphasizes a future duration?
options: She will be working for the next three months.
questions.explanation: For the next three months identifies a future period.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly shows parallel future actions?
options: While you are studying, I will be cooking.
While you will study, I cook yesterday.
While you studied, I will cooking.
While you study, I was cooking.
questions.explanation: One future-continuous clause establishes future time for both linked actions.

questions.question: Which is a polite inquiry about a future plan?
options: Will you be joining us tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Future continuous makes the inquiry polite and indirect.

questions.question: Which sentence is an assumption about the present?
options: They will be preparing for the meeting right now.
questions.explanation: Future continuous can express a confident present assumption.

questions.question: Does “be” change with different subjects in future continuous?
options: No, it always remains be after will.
questions.explanation: Will is followed by the base form be for every subject.

questions.question: Choose the correct positive sentence.
questions.explanation: The order is subject + will be + verb-ing.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative sentence.
options: I do not will be attending.
questions.explanation: Put not between will and be.

questions.question: What is the contraction of “will not”?
questions.explanation: Will not contracts irregularly to won't.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative contraction.
questions.explanation: Won't be must be followed by the -ing verb.

questions.question: Choose the correctly inverted question.
questions.explanation: Move will before the subject.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses future continuous?
options: She will has been working tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will be working has the correct order and forms.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly shows parallel future actions?
options: I will study while they are cooking.
I will be studying while they are cooking.
I studied while they are cooking.
I am studying while they will cook.
questions.explanation: The future-continuous clause establishes future time for both parallel actions.

questions.question: Which is a polite inquiry?
options: Will you be joining us for dinner tomorrow?
questions.explanation: It is both a question and the target future-continuous form.

questions.question: What is the negative of “They will be playing soccer”?
options: They will not be playing soccer.
questions.explanation: Put not between will and be; keep playing.

questions.question: Which sentence uses future continuous incorrectly?
options: I will be watching TV tonight.
They will be arriving next week.
I will be knowing the answer tomorrow.
She will be studying all day.
questions.explanation: Know is stative; use I will know.

questions.question: Correct “He will be owning a car next year.”
options: He will own a car next year.
He will be own a car next year.
He owns be a car next year.
He will owning a car next year.
questions.explanation: Own expresses possession and normally uses simple future.

questions.question: Complete: “At this time tomorrow I ___ to New York.”
questions.explanation: Use will be plus flying.

questions.question: Complete the negative: “They ___ on the project tomorrow.”
questions.explanation: The negative structure is will not be + verb-ing.

questions.question: Complete: “While you are studying, I ___ dinner.”
questions.explanation: Will be cooking is the future action parallel to are studying.

questions.question: Complete: “She ___ the meeting next week.”
questions.explanation: Will be attending is the correct form.

questions.question: Choose the contracted form of “She will be attending.”
questions.explanation: She will contracts to she'll.

questions.question: Complete the question: “___ they ___ us for lunch tomorrow?”
questions.explanation: Question order is will + subject + be + verb-ing.

questions.question: What does the first speaker ask Dan about?
questions.explanation: The first question asks whether Dan will be using his bike.

questions.question: When does the speaker ask about the bike?
questions.explanation: The dialogue says this afternoon.

questions.question: Can the speaker take Dan’s bike?
questions.explanation: Dan says, “You can’t take it.”

questions.question: What will Dan be doing tonight?
questions.explanation: Dan says he’ll be going out with his friends.

questions.question: Which place might Dan pass?
questions.explanation: The speaker asks whether he will be passing the post office.

questions.question: What does the speaker want Dan to get?
questions.explanation: The request is to get a package.

questions.question: What does Dan hope about the package?
questions.explanation: Dan hopes the package is not heavy.

questions.question: Which question is quoted from the dialogue?
options: Will you be using your bike this afternoon?
Did you use your bike yesterday?
questions.explanation: It is the opening future-continuous question.

questions.question: What is the full form of “I’ll be going out”?
questions.explanation: I'll contracts I will.

questions.question: Which phrase expresses probability?
questions.explanation: Most probably indicates likelihood rather than certainty.

questions.question: Why does the speaker use future-continuous questions?
options: To ask politely about expected future activity
questions.explanation: The questions politely inquire about Dan’s plans.

questions.question: Choose the correct structure from the dialogue.
options: Will you be passing the post office?
Will you passing the post office?
questions.explanation: Use will + subject + be + verb-ing.

questions.question: Complete: “We ___ to our new apartment at this time on Thursday.”
questions.explanation: At this time on Thursday calls for an action in progress.

questions.question: Complete: “This time next week Susan ___ football.”
questions.explanation: Will be playing matches the specified future moment.

questions.question: Choose the correct question opening.
questions.explanation: Invert will and Sam after where.

questions.question: Complete: “She ___ a red dress.”
questions.explanation: Will be wearing is the target form.

questions.question: Choose the natural contraction.
questions.explanation: She'll means she will.

questions.question: Complete: “Everyone ___ at that hour.”
questions.explanation: Use will be + sleeping.

questions.question: Complete: “Fred ___ as a lead developer in four years’ time.”
questions.explanation: The future period uses will be working.

questions.question: Complete: “At eight tomorrow morning, I ___ my son to daycare.”
questions.explanation: The exact future time calls for will be taking.

questions.question: Which question is correctly formed?
options: What will you be doing at 7 p.m. tomorrow?
What you will be doing tomorrow?
What will be you doing tomorrow?
What do you will doing tomorrow?
